change: Ungrouped Parquet aggregate tasks now use generic CPU owned reduction continuations for batch updates and checkpoint merges. New owned task and fan-in entrypoints retain partials through asynchronous transport and expose final ownership; plain functions release at caller transfer. Partial owners are released after reduction or drained failure. Custom transport returns are detached under admission even when object identity is unchanged, covering in-place mutation for aggregate and window task boundaries.

edgeCases: real Parquet median/sum/count with null input across two concurrent tasks
delayed transport holds shared pool reservations
transport rejection cleans all state and partial owners
owned final output remains charged until release
in-place enlarged median checkpoint rejects under 64 KiB and cleans up
in-place enlarged window row rejects under 64 KiB and cleans up

compatibility: Checkpoint merge capability remains optional for third-party backends.
Owned scalar vector-shape/expression contracts now apply to task aggregation; unsupported shapes raise the generic typed capability error.
Generic final output-row budget checks now apply to owned task finalization.
remaining: Grouped Parquet task state and result shaping remain on legacy functions and need owned integration.
Task topology/metadata and predicate/partition-column scratch require admission review.
Allocation inside a custom callback is external; admission bounds the retained copy after callback return.
Full mixed-operator constrained acceptance remains open.
